ai.description: This lizard reaches 75 mm snout-vent length. It is sandy-brown with distinct white longitudinal stripes and possesses characteristic fringed toes and a sharply pointed snout.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Acanthodactylus blanfordii* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, enlarged subocular scale that reaches the lip, separating it from similar Indian lacertids.
ai.habitat: Acanthodactylus blanfordii inhabits arid, sandy desert plains and semi-desert regions of the Indian subcontinent, typically featuring sparse xerophytic vegetation.
ai.behavior: Blanford's fringe-toed lizard is primarily diurnal, actively foraging across sandy substrates during the day while using its fringed toes to navigate loose dunes efficiently.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Acanthodactylus blanfordii* is oviparous, typically laying a clutch of 2–4 eggs. Breeding occurs during the spring and summer months in its arid Indian habitats.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Acanthodactylus blanfordii* is found in the arid regions of Rajasthan and Gujarat, typically inhabiting sandy desert landscapes at low elevations.
